studies.label: University card-game character design course

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract (total participants); PDF p. 4, section 3.2 (all selected students randomly assigned); PDF p. 9, Figure 8 (initial arm labels, inspected in the PDF image) and Table 1 (analyzed Group and N cells). Quote contains separate excerpts in that order.
counts_source.quote:
involving 120 undergraduate students assigned to three conditions:
GAI-SDTS Group (N=40) GAI Group (N=40) TDL Group (N=40)
(1) GAI-SDTS 40
(2) GAI 40
(3) TDL 40

arms.name: GAI-SDTS
arms.description: Generative AI-supported learning with Structured Design Thinking Strategy: Deepseek and Dreamina plus the Double Diamond-Based Design Operation Sheet, guiding Discover, Define, Develop, and Deliver. Same operational AI training as GAI (PDF pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).

arms.name: GAI
arms.description: Generative AI-supported learning without the strategy: free use of the same Deepseek and Dreamina tools without structured design-thinking guidance. Same operational AI training as GAI-SDTS (PDF pp. 5-9, sections 3.3-3.5).

arms.name: TDL
arms.description: Traditional Design Learning: printed materials and online references, hand-drawn sketches, and conventional digital tools such as Photoshop, without generative AI or an explicit design-thinking strategy (PDF pp. 4-5, sections 3.2-3.3).

studies.task: Independently create a distinctive card-game character with clear personality traits, progressing through exploration, definition, creation, and final presentation.

ai_tool.name: Deepseek and Dreamina
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, section 3.3 names both tools and describes text dialogue, text-to-image and image-to-image generation; PDF pp. 6-8, Figures 3-7 illustrate use. No release year or experiment-wide model version is specified.

estimates.outcome: Design achievement: composite expert rating of final character artwork
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Expert assessment of each student’s final character artwork. The rubric includes Technical Skill, Adherence to Theme, Composition and Design, Creativity, and Detail Quality and Workload; each dimension uses a five-point scale from lowest to highest. Two design instructors independently rated anonymized, randomly ordered submissions. The paper reports a composite design-achievement score but does not explain aggregation across dimensions or raters (PDF p. 8, section 3.4; PDF p. 9, Table 1).

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, Table 1, Post-test, GAI row; cells Group, N, Mean, S.D.
PDF p. 9, Table 1, Post-test, TDL row; cells Group, N, Mean, S.D.
PDF p. 9, section 4.1, Tukey’s HSD post hoc comparisons paragraph (line wraps and whitespace normalized).

estimates.notes: The composite measures broad design-output quality, including a Creativity dimension, so it is coded usefulness. Higher scores mean better design achievement. The analysis uses one final-work score per student; Table 1 reports students, not separate instructor ratings. The p-value is the printed Tukey HSD pairwise bound; no pairwise test statistic or degrees of freedom are printed, so test is null. The omnibus ANOVA is not a statistic for this two-arm contrast. Printed means, SDs, counts, and p-values are retained despite the unresolved reporting inconsistency. No mean difference, SE, CI, or standardized effect has been calculated. n_total is null because the paper does not print a total for this two-arm contrast. Grading occurs at course end on artwork produced with AI available, without a new unassisted task; timing is immediate (PDF p. 9, section 3.5; PDF p. 11, section 5.1).

open_items: PDF p. 9, Table 1 and section 4.1: the printed arm means, SDs, and sample sizes appear inconsistent with the omnibus ANOVA and the reported significance of every Tukey pairwise comparison. This concern is also recorded in the reconciled form. Corrected values cannot be established from the PDF; underlying scores or author-confirmed analysis output are needed. No replacement statistics were inferred.

PDF p. 8, section 3.4 and PDF p. 9, Table 1: separate results for Technical Skill, Adherence to Theme, Composition and Design, Creativity, and Detail Quality and Workload are not printed. The rule for combining dimensions and the two instructors’ ratings is not stated. No separate dimension contrast can be extracted.

PDF p. 9, section 4.1 and Table 1: no pairwise mean difference, standard error, confidence interval, standardized effect, HSD statistic, or degrees of freedom is printed. The paper also prints no participant total specifically for any two-arm contrast; those totals remain null.

PDF pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2: the authors call the study quasi-experimental but explicitly describe random assignment of individual students and reorganization across sampled classes. Random sequence generation and allocation implementation are not described.

PDF p. 4, Figure 1 labels design achievement as one-way ANCOVA, while PDF p. 9, section 4 and Table 1 specify one-way ANOVA. Extraction follows the Results and Table 1; the diagram discrepancy is unexplained.

PDF p. 7, Figure 6 shows Dreamina 图片 4.5 (Images 4.5), and PDF p. 8, Figure 7 shows 图片 4.1 (Images 4.1); labels were inspected in enlarged PDF image crops. These illustrations do not establish experiment-wide versions. The Deepseek model version and release years of the actual tools/models used are not given, so ai_tool.year is null.

The external Supplementary Table S1 was not independently read in this extraction. It is identified as the design operation sheet in PDF p. 5, section 3.3, with a link on PDF p. 14. The existing forms/data/c566.json inventory describes a previously inspected materials-only DOCX with no outcome data. Current urllib requests to the named Frontiers supplemental-data API and Figshare article API both failed with WinError 10013. No supplement-only statistics are assumed.
notes: Extracted independently by B on 2026-10-11. The complete markdown conversion, including the final references, was read in chunks; all figures and tables were inspected in the PDF, and every cited page was extracted with PyMuPDF. Table 1 was recovered with find_tables. The PDF has no appended supplement or embedded attachment. Eligible-outcome statistic inventory: Table 1 (PDF p. 9) prints GAI-SDTS N = 40, M = 20.90, SD = 7.64; GAI N = 40, M = 18.65, SD = 7.41; TDL N = 40, M = 16.13, SD = 6.85. Section 4.1 prints a Tukey HSD p < 0.001 for each of the three pairwise comparisons; these are transcribed in the estimates. Additional outcome-related statistics are diagnostic or omnibus rather than pairwise effects: PDF p. 9, section 4.1, "The ANOVA revealed a statistically significant effect of instructional condition on design achievement, F = 43.28, p < 0.001"; same section, "The assumption of homogeneity of variances was tested using Levene’s test, and the result was non-significant (p > 0.05)"; PDF p. 8, section 3.4, "Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Kendall’s W, which yielded a value of 0.94 (p < 0.001)". No omnibus F or inter-rater reliability statistic is attached to a pairwise contrast. All arm-level descriptive statistics retain their printed precision in the source quotes. The study total and initial arm counts agree with the analyzed arm counts; no exclusions or attrition are reported. Cluster sampling of existing classes was followed by individual random assignment, so sampling classes are not coded as randomized clusters. TDL is ordinary design coursework, so AI comparisons with TDL are ai_vs_bau. GAI-SDTS versus free GAI use is ai_design, with the proposed structured configuration as treatment. Deepseek also provided open dialogue, ideation, and refinement; Dreamina generated and refined images. The comparisons share participants and arms and are not independent studies. No shared sample with another paper, preregistration, across-people diversity result, or output produced after AI removal is reported. The raw-data availability statement (PDF p. 14) promises author provision but supplies no public dataset link.
